00 — Overview

What We're Building

A premium, SEO-dominant hemp e-commerce brand built on top of your brother's fulfillment operation at 10dollarcartridge.com. You take the orders, he ships them. Your differentiation lives in three areas: brand positioning (premium, science-forward vs. budget), user experience (luxury feel, friction-free checkout), and content authority (becoming the go-to reference site that AI search cites).

Model

Dropship

You collect orders + payment. Forward order details to brother. He fulfills. You keep the margin spread.

Moat

Content & Brand

Deep educational content builds domain authority, earns AI citations, and converts high-intent organic traffic.

Revenue

E-Commerce + SEO

Direct sales via Stripe, long-term compounding returns from search rankings and AI answer inclusion.

01 — Legal & Compliance

Non-Negotiables Before You Write a Line of Code

⚠ Stripe Hemp/THC Policy: Stripe allows hemp-derived CBD products but may flag or terminate accounts selling THC-containing products, even federally legal THCa/Delta-8. You need a backup processor ready on day one.
Payment Stack

Primary + Fallback

Primary: Stripe (with proper hemp MCC codes — use MCC 5912 or specialty retail). Describe products as hemp-derived botanicals in your Stripe account. Keep product descriptions compliant — never use "THC" in payment descriptors.

Fallback (Day 1): Set up Authorize.net or NMI via a high-risk merchant account. Costs more per transaction (~3.5%) but won't disappear overnight.

Optional: Crypto via Coinbase Commerce as a no-chargeback option popular in this market.

Site-Wide Requirements

Legal Checklist

Every page must include the 2018 Farm Bill disclaimer. Required pages:

  • ✓ Age gate (21+ modal — hard block)
  • ✓ Terms & Conditions
  • ✓ Privacy Policy (CCPA + GDPR)
  • ✓ Lab Results page (COA uploads)
  • ✓ Age Verification Policy
  • ✓ No FDA evaluate/cure claims anywhere
  • ✓ State restriction list (some states ban Delta-8)
Delta-8 State Restrictions: Before checkout, check the shipping state against a blocked-states list. States currently restricting Delta-8 include Alaska, Colorado, Delaware, Idaho, Iowa, Minnesota, Montana, New York, Nevada, North Dakota, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont, Utah, and others. This must be enforced at checkout — not just disclosed.
02 — Technology Stack

The Right Tools for the Job

Chosen for SEO performance, developer velocity, and long-term maintainability. Every choice has a reason.

Frontend

Next.js 14 (App Router) React 18 TypeScript Tailwind CSS Framer Motion Zustand React Query

Next.js App Router gives you RSC (React Server Components) for zero-JS product pages — critical for Core Web Vitals and SEO. Static generation for blog posts, dynamic for cart/checkout.

Backend & Database

Next.js API Routes PostgreSQL Prisma ORM Redis (Upstash) Zod

Prisma gives type-safe DB access. Redis via Upstash for session caching, rate limiting, and cart state. All in one Next.js monorepo — no separate backend to manage.

Auth & Accounts

NextAuth.js v5 JWT Sessions Email Magic Links Google OAuth

Passwordless login via magic email links lowers signup friction dramatically. Google OAuth as one-click option. Age verification stored in session.

Content / Blog

Sanity.io CMS MDX Portable Text Schema.org

Sanity is the best headless CMS for SEO content. GROQ queries are fast, the Studio is beautiful, and the portable text blocks support rich structured content with custom components.

Infrastructure

Vercel Supabase (Postgres) Cloudflare (DNS + CDN) Resend (Email) Uploadthing

Why Not Shopify?

Shopify is the obvious choice for e-commerce — but it carries real risk in this industry. Shopify has terminated hemp/THC stores without warning. You'd lose your entire store, domain, customer data, and SEO overnight. Building custom gives you control, portability, and full ownership of every asset. The build investment pays back in one bad Shopify termination event avoided.

04 — Data Model

Database Schema (Prisma)

User
model User {
  id            String    @id @default(cuid())
  email         String    @unique
  name          String?
  emailVerified DateTime?
  ageVerified   Boolean   @default(false)
  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
  orders        Order[]
  reviews       Review[]
  addresses     Address[]
}
Product
model Product {
  id           String    @id @default(cuid())
  slug         String    @unique
  name         String
  description  String    @db.Text
  category     Category  @relation(...)
  variants     Variant[]
  images       Json      // [{url, alt, isPrimary}]
  effects      String[]  // sleep, focus, pain...
  strain       StrainType // indica/sativa/hybrid
  thcaPercent  Float?
  terpenes     Json?
  coaUrl       String?  // lab results PDF
  publishedAt  DateTime?
  reviews      Review[]
  active       Boolean  @default(true)
}
Order
model Order {
  id              String       @id
  userId          String?
  user            User?        @relation(...)
  stripePaymentId String       @unique
  status          OrderStatus  // pending|paid|fulfilled|shipped
  items           OrderItem[]
  shippingAddress Json
  shippingState   String       // for restriction check
  subtotal        Int          // cents
  total           Int          // cents
  trackingNumber  String?
  forwardedAt     DateTime?    // when sent to brother
  createdAt       DateTime     @default(now())
}
Content (Blog)
// Managed in Sanity CMS

model ArticleAnalytics {

  slug       String   @unique
  views      Int      @default(0)
  avgTimeOnPage Int   @default(0)
  topKeyword String?

}

05 — Fulfillment Integration

Order Flow with Your Brother

The core of this business is the handoff from your payment to his fulfillment. Automate as much as possible to avoid manual error.

Automated Order Flow

// When Stripe webhook fires on payment_intent.succeeded:

async function handleSuccessfulPayment(paymentIntent: Stripe.PaymentIntent) {
  // 1. Create order in your database
  const order = await prisma.order.create({ data: { ... } })

  // 2. Forward to brother via email (Resend)
  await resend.emails.send({
    from: 'orders@yourstore.com',
    to: 'brother@10dollarcartridge.com',
    subject: `New Order #${order.id}`,
    react: FulfillmentEmailTemplate({ order }),
  })

  // 3. Send customer confirmation email
  await resend.emails.send({
    from: 'hello@yourstore.com',
    to: order.customerEmail,
    react: OrderConfirmationTemplate({ order }),
  })

  // 4. Mark order as "forwarded"
  await prisma.order.update({
    where: { id: order.id },
    data: { forwardedAt: new Date() }
  })
}
Fulfillment Email to Brother

What the Order Email Contains

The email sent to your brother should be a clean, printable order sheet with: Customer name, shipping address, product names (matching his SKUs), quantities, any variant details (strain, size), order reference number, and a direct link to place the order on his site if you prefer he manually processes it. No pricing — he doesn't need to know your margin.

Pro Tip: Consider building a simple admin panel at /admin/orders where you can view order status, manually update tracking numbers, and your brother can optionally log in to mark orders as shipped. This removes email as a single point of failure.
06 — User Experience Design

High-End UX That Converts

Your competitive advantage vs. 10DC is sophistication. Same products, radically different experience — think Goop meets MedMen. The brand should feel like a premium wellness destination, not a vape shop website.

Brand Direction

Aesthetic

Organic Luxury

Color palette: Deep forest green, warm cream, gold accents, charcoal. Typography: Serif display font (Playfair Display or Canela) + clean sans-serif body. Photography: editorial, lifestyle, botanical. Zero neon, zero street art, zero "420" tropes.

Positioning

Science-Forward Wellness

Lead with cannabinoid education, lab results, and effect-based shopping. Customers shop by "I want to sleep better" not by product category. Position your brand as the resource they trust before buying.

Key UX Features

  • Effect-Based Shop Filter — "Sleep / Focus / Euphoria / Pain Relief" filter bar on shop page. Maps to product tags. High conversion feature.
  • Strain Type Filter — Indica / Sativa / Hybrid with visual icons
  • Sticky Cart — Slide-out cart drawer, never leave the page to add items
  • Terpene Profiles — Visual terpene wheel on product pages (beautiful + educational)
  • Product Quiz — "Find Your Perfect Product" 5-question quiz → product recommendation
  • Lab Results Inline — COA PDF viewer embedded on each product page, not just a link
  • One-Page Checkout — Stripe Elements embedded directly, no redirect
  • Age Gate — Beautiful full-screen gate, stored in localStorage + session
07 — SEO & AI Search Strategy

Becoming the Source AI Cites

AI search (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) cites sources with high topical authority, clear structured data, and comprehensive coverage of a niche. Your content strategy targets the exact questions people ask before buying hemp products.

Content Architecture

Tier 1 — Pillar Pages

Comprehensive Guides (3000–5000 words)

One definitive guide per major topic. Updated quarterly. These earn backlinks and become the "source of truth" for AI systems.

  • → "Complete Guide to THCa: What It Is, Effects, Legality"
  • → "Hemp-Derived Cannabinoids Explained: Delta-8, Delta-9, THCa"
  • → "How to Choose Hemp Flower: A Buyer's Guide"
  • → "Terpenes 101: The Complete Reference"
  • → "Hemp vs. Marijuana: Legal Differences Explained"
Tier 2 — Supporting Articles

Targeted Blog Posts (800–1500 words)

Long-tail keyword targeting. Cluster around pillar topics. Internally link to pillar pages and relevant products.

  • → "THCa Diamonds vs. Badder: Which is Right for You?"
  • → "Best Indica Strains for Sleep 2026"
  • → "Is Delta-8 THC Legal in [State]?" (one per restricted state)
  • → "What is Live Rosin? How It's Made"
  • → "THCa Percentage: What the Lab Results Actually Mean"

Technical SEO Implementation

// app/learn/[slug]/page.tsx — Article page with full SEO

export async function generateMetadata({ params }) {
  const article = await getArticle(params.slug)
  return {
    title: article.seoTitle,
    description: article.metaDescription,
    openGraph: {
      title: article.seoTitle,
      description: article.metaDescription,
      images: [{ url: article.ogImage }],
      type: 'article',
      publishedTime: article.publishedAt,
      modifiedTime: article.updatedAt,
    },
    alternates: { canonical: `https://yourstore.com/learn/${params.slug}` }
  }
}

// JSON-LD structured data (required for AI citations)
const jsonLd = {
  '@context': 'https://schema.org',
  '@type': 'Article',
  headline: article.title,
  datePublished: article.publishedAt,
  dateModified: article.updatedAt,
  author: { '@type': 'Person', name: article.author },
  publisher: { '@type': 'Organization', name: 'Your Brand' },
  mainEntityOfPage: article.canonicalUrl,
  // FAQ schema for question-based articles — key for AI snippets
  hasPart: article.faqs?.map(faq => ({
    '@type': 'Question',
    name: faq.question,
    acceptedAnswer: { '@type': 'Answer', text: faq.answer }
  }))
}

The AI Search Citation Playbook

AI systems (Perplexity, ChatGPT, Google SGE) pull from sources that demonstrate:

  • Comprehensive coverage — answer every sub-question within a topic
  • Structured data — FAQ schema, HowTo schema, Article schema on every page
  • Author credentials — visible author bios with expertise signals
  • Source citations within your content — cite studies, link to COAs, reference the Farm Bill
  • Update frequency — articles with recent "Last Updated" dates are heavily favored
  • Site trust signals — About page, Contact, Privacy Policy, real business info
  • Internal linking — tightly interconnected content signals topical authority
08 — Stripe Integration

Payment Implementation

// app/api/checkout/create-session/route.ts

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { items, shippingAddress } = await req.json()

  // 1. Validate shipping state against restricted list
  const restricted = checkStateRestrictions(items, shippingAddress.state)
  if (restricted.length > 0) {
    return Response.json({
      error: `Sorry, we cannot ship ${restricted.join(', ')} to ${shippingAddress.state}.`
    }, { status: 400 })
  }

  // 2. Calculate total server-side (NEVER trust client)
  const products = await prisma.variant.findMany({ where: { id: { in: items.map(i => i.variantId) } } })
  const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => {
    const product = products.find(p => p.id === item.variantId)
    return sum + (product.priceCents * item.quantity)
  }, 0)

  // 3. Create Stripe PaymentIntent
  const paymentIntent = await stripe.paymentIntents.create({
    amount: total,
    currency: 'usd',
    // IMPORTANT: Use descriptor that doesn't mention THC/cannabis
    statement_descriptor_suffix: 'BOTANICALS',
    metadata: {
      orderId: generateOrderId(),
      itemCount: items.length.toString(),
    }
  })

  return Response.json({ clientSecret: paymentIntent.client_secret })
}
Statement Descriptor: Set your Stripe statement descriptor to your brand name + "BOTANICALS" or "WELLNESS". Never include cannabis, hemp, THC, CBD, or weed in the statement descriptor — it increases chargeback rates and Stripe scrutiny.

Shop Core

Checkout & Payments

User Accounts
Week 6
  • Account dashboard: order history, reorder functionality
  • Saved addresses, account settings

Content Engine
Weeks 7–8
  • Sanity CMS setup: article schema, author schema, category schema
  • Blog listing page + individual article pages with full SEO
  • JSON-LD structured data on all article and product pages
  • Write first 5 pillar guides (publish immediately at launch)
  • Write first 10 supporting articles targeting low-competition keywords
  • XML sitemap + robots.txt optimized for crawl budget
  • Internal linking strategy implemented
Polish & Launch
Week 9
  • Core Web Vitals audit — target LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1, FID <100ms
  • Lighthouse score >90 on all pages
  • Mobile UX final pass
  • Legal pages: Terms, Privacy, Age Policy, Refund Policy
  • Google Search Console + Analytics 4 setup
  • Stripe live mode testing with small real transactions
  • Soft launch → share with network for first reviews

Recommended First Action

Before writing a line of code, do three things: (1) Register your domain and brand name — pick something that signals premium wellness, not budget vape. (2) Open your Stripe account and configure it for hemp/botanical products immediately so it ages before you go live. (3) Write your first 3 pillar SEO articles and publish them on launch day — fresh domains need content immediately to start earning trust with Google.

  • Brand name ideas: something with "Verdant", "Canopy", "Grove", "Terrain", "Pura", "Alder" — botanical, premium, memorable
  • Get a high-risk merchant account application started in parallel with Stripe setup
  • Use AI tools (Claude) to help draft the initial 5 pillar content pieces — but edit heavily for brand voice and accuracy
